Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The failure is related to incorrect behavior of binary operators involving node-sets as described in the current bug report, which mentions the XPath specification for node-set comparisons: When both operands are node-sets, the comparison is true if there exists at least one node in each set where the comparison on their string-values is true.

The failing test `testNodeSetOperations()` tests an XPath expression `$array > 0`, which implicates comparison involving node-sets or collections.

Investigating the code in `CoreOperationEqual.computeValue(EvalContext)` shows it delegates to a method called `equal(context, args[0], args[1])`.

The `equal(EvalContext, Expression, Expression)` method in `CoreOperationCompare` computes the two sides and then attempts to handle node-set (or collection) and other types of operand conversions and comparisons.

Crucially, if either side is a `Collection`, it is converted to an `Iterator`. Then, if one side is an `Iterator` and the other is not, it calls `contains(Iterator, Object)`. If both sides are `Iterator`, it calls `findMatch(Iterator, Iterator)`.

The `contains(Iterator, Object)` simply checks if any element in the iterator matches the given value using `equal(element, value)`.

However, from this code snippet, the behavior of `findMatch(Iterator, Iterator)`, which should perform the node-set to node-set comparisons as per the XPath spec, is unknown. The bug likely lies in that method or in how each element's comparison is evaluated.

The symptom described in the bug report that binary operators involving node-sets do not behave correctly is consistent with an incorrect implementation of `findMatch(Iterator, Iterator)` or possibly the `equal(Object, Object)` method used for element comparisons.

Since the test case involves `$array > 0`, the comparison should adhere to the numeric comparison rules across node-set string-values, thus possibly the current code is not correctly performing per XPath spec.

Recent reports are unrelated or not directly relevant.

Hence, the root cause is that in `CoreOperationCompare.equal()` logic for node-set comparisons, the `findMatch(Iterator, Iterator)` implementation or the equality check on the string-values of nodes is either missing or incorrect, resulting in the failing test and reported bad binary operator behavior for node-sets.

Next, analyzing the implementation of `findMatch` and the underlying `equal(Object, Object)` will likely confirm the issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
